correctness.rationale: For normalized surface measure on S_+^{d-1}, Gaussian absolute-coordinate representation gives exact first moments m_d=Gamma(d/2)/(sqrt(pi)Gamma((d+1)/2)) and covariance eigenvalues lambda_perp=(1-2/pi)/d, lambda_parallel=[1+(d-1)2/pi-d^2m_d^2]/d. The affine L2 reproducing kernel is 1+(a-m_d1)^T Sigma^{-1}(X-m_d1); gamma expansion yields d lambda_parallel->c=1-3/pi>0. For any sequence with max_i a_i->0, a triangular-array joint Lindeberg CLT for the centered perpendicular coordinate combination B_d and normalized radial-fluctuation T_d gives independent Gaussian terms with variances (1-2/pi)(1-theta^2) and c. Delta-method expansion of ||Z|| and uniform L2 bound on K/√d justify taking absolute expectations, proving Λ_d(a)/√d−F(theta_d)->0 with F(theta)=sqrt(2/pi)*sqrt((1-theta²)/(1-2/pi)+(theta-sqrt(2/pi))²/(1-3/pi)). F(theta)^2 is strictly convex on [0,1], endpoint comparison gives unique maximum at 0 and constant C*=3.27783611857179. Sparse but delocalized k_d-supported vectors with k_d->inf, k_d/d->0 realize it, proving only a global liminf norm lower bound, NOT a full operator-norm limit. Independently checked eigenvalue inversion in dimensions 3,6,15,70,128 and numeric constant.

value.rationale: Affine L2 projection onto a fundamental positive spherical sector is a natural approximation operator with an unexplained high-dimensional L∞ amplification profile. The formula and rigidity isolate the dependence on delocalized support and provide a sharp, attainable lower bound for the global operator norm. The theorem explicitly refuses to extrapolate to fixed spikes or nondiffuse directions, retaining mathematical relevance as a self-contained limiting law.
